questions.q: In the chapter's static risk scoring table, a DDL change requiring an exclusive lock receives a base score of:
questions.explain: The static_rules dictionary maps ("ddl", "exclusive") to 40 — the highest base score in the table.

questions.q: Given the final risk score, what action does the scorer select for each tier?
options: LOW → block; MEDIUM → escalate; HIGH → defer; CRITICAL → execute immediately
LOW < 20 → execute_immediately; MEDIUM < 45 → execute_with_monitoring; HIGH < 75 → defer_to_maintenance_window; CRITICAL → block (escalate or defer 72h)
All tiers execute immediately; only logging differs
Tiers are advisory and never gate execution
questions.explain: _select_autonomous_action maps LOW to execute_immediately, MEDIUM to execute_with_monitoring, HIGH to defer_to_maintenance_window, and CRITICAL to block_and_escalate or block_and_defer_72h.

questions.q: Which statement does the chapter describe as metadata-only and trivially safe on SQL Server 2012 and later?
options: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN on a column with dependent indexed views
CREATE INDEX ... WITH (ONLINE = OFF) on a 50-million-row table
ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN with a default value
questions.explain: The chapter states that ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN with a default value is a metadata-only operation on SQL Server 2012+, while ALTER COLUMN with dependent indexed views is blocking.

questions.q: Which live-risk condition adds the largest dynamic multiplier to the change risk score?
questions.explain: The scoring code adds +0.8 when lock_wait_count > 10 — the largest of the listed multipliers, since lock accumulation means DDL may queue badly.

questions.q: The self-throttling batched migration executor reacts to AG replica lag by:
options: Pausing for an exponential backoff of 2^violations seconds (capped at 60s) and halving the batch size, within a 100–50,000 batch-size range targeting 500 ms batches
Immediately aborting the migration and rolling back all committed batches
Doubling the batch size to finish faster
Ignoring lag and continuing at the initial batch size of 1000
questions.explain: On lag violations it sleeps min(2^consecutive_violations, 60) seconds, halves the batch size, and self-tunes batch size between 100 and 50,000 toward a 500 ms target duration.
